title: Shared-Codex guard layer is process-scoped by default: four fail paths, thread/started, detach, and api.rs all still bypass the attachment
outcome:
Round-10 review. THE SYSTEMIC FINDING — the individual sites are symptoms.

Every per-session guard in the shared-Codex layer keys on the app-server PROCESS, and the process outlives any one attachment. The epoch (tm-c7l) introduced CodexAttachment and converted the sites reviewers named in rounds 8-9. Round 10 named FOUR MORE. Point-fixing is not converging.

STILL PROCESS-SCOPED (verified):
- codex.rs:1250, 1383, 1658, 1733 — RuntimeToken::Codex(...) on waiter/turn-start failure paths. A dead attachment can still fail its replacement's turn (the [deleted:tm-t78] class, which I only half-fixed).
- codex_events.rs:269 + :413 — thread/started guards on the PROCESS and then calls the UNCONDITIONAL set_external_session_id. The tm-c7l identity clobber, still open. (tm-c7l REOPENED.)
- session_runtime.rs:148/155/206 — SharedCodexSessionHandle has no generation; remove_locked_session removes unconditionally; detach_async runs it later. A deferred detach wipes the LIVE attachment. ([deleted:tm-92r], upgraded to P1.)
- api.rs — attachment check, lock released, then unconditional clear_runtime + fail_turn. Check-then-act; tm-0og survives in a narrower window.

WHY THIS IS ONE BEAD, NOT FIVE: the defect is that the attachment is OPTIONAL. Every guard that forgets it silently degrades to 'any attachment on this process', which always matches. Fixing named sites one round at a time has produced a HALF-APPLIED epoch — some paths attachment-guarded, some process-guarded — and inconsistent guards are precisely how [deleted:tm-dpa] happened.

CONVERGENT FIX — make the attachment unavoidable rather than hunting for places that forgot it:
1. SharedCodexSessionHandle gains attachment_generation; remove_locked_session becomes compare-and-remove. (closes [deleted:tm-92r])
2. SharedCodexSessionState carries its CodexAttachment, so the EVENT dispatcher can guard identity writes by attachment instead of process. (closes tm-c7l's second door)
3. Sweep the remaining RuntimeToken::Codex(..) on per-session paths to RuntimeToken::CodexAttachment. Leave it ONLY on runtime-exit fan-out, which legitimately must match every attachment on a dead process.
4. api.rs: one atomic attachment-guarded teardown instead of check-then-act.

After (1)-(4) there is no process-level guard left on any per-session path, so there is nothing further of this class to find.
acceptance: grep shows RuntimeToken::Codex( remaining ONLY on runtime-exit fan-out; every per-session write and removal in the shared-Codex layer is attachment-guarded; tests cover the deferred-detach wipe and the stale thread/started clobber.
